title: Home
text:
Welcome to my portfolio for MUSA 5080: Public Policy Analytics at the University of Pennsylvania.😄
This site documents my work in the Master of Urban Spatial Analytics program — weekly notes, course assignments, and a final project applying data analysis to urban policy questions.



I’m a student in the MUSA program at Penn. My background is in hands-on GIS fieldwork, site analysis, and 3D imagery processing, and I’m interested in smart cities and walkability.




Weekly Notes — what I’m learning each week
Assignments — analyses completed for the course
About — more background and how to reach me

title: Week 1: Getting Set Up
text:
Key Concepts
Three places a file can live:

My computer — where I edit
GitHub.com — where it’s stored
My live site — what the world sees

What is a website?
A folder of .html files -> Quarto
& A computer that is always on. -> Github Pages (free!)
Quarto
file contain .qmd to modify
l>Quarto(machine) - RENDER
L>.htmi(webpage)
What happen in the machine?

Read file from Top to Bottom
Find code chunks
Sends them to R, gets results back
Glues text + results into HTML

Antomy of .qmd
YAML (title, date)
Markdown (.md)
Code chucks (’’‘, {}, library(tidycensis), 2+2,’’’)
Files+Folders
Who is the file for?
For me (a page I worte)
index.qmd
about.qmd
weekly_notes/*.qmd
assignments/.qmd
For the Machines
quarto.yml (settings for whole website)
_freeze/ -> quarto
Rproj ->Rstudio
.gitignore -> Github
Renviron -> R (secrets)
docs/ -> The Internet
Index
Website Rule: Ask for a folder, you get that folder’s index.html
YOURNAME.github.io/ -> docs/index.htmi
/weekly_notes -> docs/weekly_notes/index.html
Git-> version traker, invisible, run on your computer
Github.com -> Website that stores a copy of your folder
Github desktop -> Buttons that tell get what to do
Commit -> “save a labeled snapshot” (live on your computer)
Push -> “send my snapshot to Github”
R script
Code Only
Sandbox

The loop: Edit → Save → Render → Commit → Push → wait → refresh

title: About
text: I was born and raised in Hong Kong and moved to the U.S. as a first-generation college student to pursue higher education. I studied Urban Studies and GIS at UC San Diego, where I fell in love with using spatial data to address real-world challenges like walkability, pedestrian safety, and wildfire risk. What drew me to urban spatial analytics is its power to combine data science, mapping, and programming to make cities more equitable, safe, and resilient. Through MUSA, I’m excited to dive into predictive modeling and urban informatics to advance sustainable transportation and hazard mitigation. My goal is to work as a GIS analyst using data to build better urban systems!
